reasons: F01, F02: a material weakness specifically in revenue, which is the area most often manipulated in misstatements.
F06, F05: a reported disagreement with the accountants together with an auditor change within two years. This combination is a strong red flag for disputes over accounting treatment.
F16: an SEC inquiry or investigation is disclosed.
F23, F21, F16 (R16): went public via a SPAC or reverse merger within 3 years and raised or is planning to raise capital. Gatekeeping is weak and there is an incentive to inflate results.
F11, F12: material related-party transactions and one customer at 36% of revenue. Related-party or round-trip revenue is possible.
F14, F20: a CEO/CFO change during the year and incentive pay tied to revenue or EPS.

R04, R02, R09: sales grew about 74x from a tiny base, and the gross margin index of 57.7 shows margins collapsing. The M-score of 87.8 is far above -1.78, but most of it comes from SGI on an early-stage revenue base.
R03, R13, F22: the asset quality index rose to 1.84 and soft assets make up 93% of total assets after a major acquisition. Goodwill and intangibles give room to manipulate valuations.
R07, R19: leverage rose about 9.4x, and operating cash flow covers only 28% of net income, so earnings are not backed by cash.
F03, F24: no ICFR auditor attestation and no CAMs, so external scrutiny is limited.
